input.note:
Cause: Port mismatch between the storefront-web Service and the 3.0 pods. The 3.0 container now listens on 0.0.0.0:3000 (pod log line "http server listening on 0.0.0.0:3000"), but the Service in shop-web still forwards to the old port, so ingress-nginx has no reachable upstream and returns 502. Pods show Running/Ready because the readiness probe hits the container directly (GET /healthz 200), which hides the Service-level break. The OpenTelemetry ECONNREFUSED errors in the logs are unrelated noise against otel-collector.observability.svc:4317 and do not affect the HTTP listener.

Evidence:
- shop-web pods storefront-web-* are Running, ready=true, image storefront-web:3.0.0, 0 restarts.
- Pod logs show the server bound to :3000 and serving /healthz 200, i.e. the app itself is healthy.
- Symptom (ingress-nginx 502) with healthy ready pods is the classic Service targetPort / containerPort mismatch described in the debugging guide: "Verify that the pod's containerPort matches the Service's targetPort" [cite: tasks/debug/debug-application/debug-pods#debugging-services-1].

Fix (owner to apply, no rollback needed):
- Update the storefront-web Service in namespace shop-web so its port's targetPort is 3000 (or, preferably, give the container a named port like http-web-svc on containerPort 3000 and set the Service targetPort to that name, per the Service port definition example) [cite: concepts/services-networking/service#field-spec-ports-0]. After kubectl apply, endpoints will repopulate and ingress-nginx will stop returning 502.
- Optional cleanup: fix or disable the OTLP exporter target otel-collector.observability.svc:4317; it is unrelated to the 502 but is spamming errors and dropping spans.
